mechanism.summary: Evaluate already-admitted numeric-leaf bitwise and shift operations directly on f64 scalar operands, rather than materializing temporary Value operands only to recover the same Number or Boolean result.
mechanism.generality: The route changes only the existing numeric-leaf executor after its bytecode and all operands have already passed the current primitive-number admission checks. It applies to every admitted leaf using ECMAScript Number bitwise, shift, exponentiation, arithmetic, or comparison operators; it has no source-path, function-name, workload, input-size, iteration-count, call-graph, or compiler-admission condition. Any non-Number operand, unsupported opcode, BigInt path, dynamic call, property access, coercion, or existing leaf-plan rejection continues through the unchanged generic VM.
semantic_risks: the direct scalar forms must exactly preserve ToInt32 and ToUint32 behavior for NaN, infinities, signed zero, fractional values, and large finite doubles
left, signed-right, and unsigned-right shifts must retain the ECMAScript five-bit count mask and signed versus unsigned result conversion
the fast result domain must preserve Boolean comparison results and Number exponentiation, remainder, and signed-zero behavior without leaking a non-Number shortcut
the implementation must not add a new bytecode classifier, eager plan construction, or dispatch probe to calls that are not already executing an admitted numeric leaf

profile_evidence.source: macOS sample 2026-07-28 /private/tmp/qjs-profile-bitops-3bit-641-v1.sample; profile-only 400x repetition of the verified SunSpider bitops-3bit-bits-in-byte hot path (wrapper SHA-256 fe2ec653fc0560c4ae9b02b0b07ac2c23258fdb2585e9b7737c5ccf524fcf2c9) executed by the runtime-equivalent post-revert release binary
profile_evidence.shared_cost: The 7,411-sample profile reaches the existing direct-leaf numeric executor on every fast3bitlookup call: try_eval_numeric_leaf has 2,147 top samples, fast_number_binary 1,070, and direct_number_binary 794. The leaf already has primitive f64 operands, but each bitwise operation still enters fast_number_binary through temporary Value::Number wrappers and drops them again.

profile_evidence.source: macOS samples 2026-07-27 /private/tmp/qjs-profile-crypto-md5-641-v3.sample and /private/tmp/qjs-profile-crypto-sha1-641-v1.sample; repeated verified SunSpider hash computations executed by the runtime-equivalent post-revert release binary
profile_evidence.shared_cost: Both independent profiles show existing numeric-leaf helpers such as safe_add and rotate operations spending material time in direct_number_binary and fast_number_binary beneath try_eval_numeric_leaf. Their outer numeric call graph remains deliberately out of scope; this unit only removes the shared scalar operation cost already present within the admitted helpers.
